content.text:
If you mean **SiriusXM satellite radio for free**, the legal options are:

1. **SiriusXM Free Trial** — SiriusXM offers free trials, usually for eligible vehicles or streaming accounts. Some trials may require registration and may convert to paid service if you add payment info. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/free-trial?utm_source=openai))  
2. **SiriusXM Free Access Plan** — SiriusXM has an ad-supported free option for some **eligible vehicles**, but it may not work in every car and does **not** include mobile-app listening. ([siriusxm.com](https://www.siriusxm.com/plans/free-access?utm_source=openai))  
3. **SiriusXM “Listen Free” events** — SiriusXM periodically opens many channels on inactive car radios for a limited time. The most recent event I found was **May 21–June 1, 2026**, so it has just ended as of today, **June 8, 2026**. ([seniordaily.com](https://www.seniordaily.com/siriusxm-free-listen-preview/?utm_source=openai))  
4. **NOAA Weather Radio** — If you meant free radio from satellites/weather services, NOAA Weather Radio is free 24/7, but it is **VHF weather radio**, not entertainment satellite radio. ([weather.gov](https://www.weather.gov/hnx/wxradio?utm_source=openai))  

If you want, tell me your **car year/make/model** or whether you want **music, talk, sports, or weather**, and I can point you to the best free option.
